newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says some U.N. members delay food plan.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says some U.N. members delay food plan.

text.p: An Iraqi official newspaper on Thursday said some United Nations members were delaying food supplies to Iraq under an oil-for-food plan signed with the world body.
Thawra, organ of the ruling Baath party, hinting that the United States was behind the delay, blamed the U.N. sanctions committee for not doing its work properly.
"It is quite clear that there are those who are working for a deliberate delay of the (plan's) implementation," the paper said.

Iraq on Tuesday complained to the U.N. Security Council that food and medical supplies under the pact were taking too long to arrive while U.N. sources said Baghdad was blocking operations on the ground.

"Stands and practices of certain members since the agreement was put into effect remind us of the overt attempts by the United States to impede the deal before it was signed (with the U.N.)," the paper said.

U.S. officials placed the entire blame on Iraq saying that it was delaying access to transportation and communications by U.N. monitors and are denying the U.N. monitors the full freedom of movement the U.N. was promised.
"Number of experts who are to monitor food distribution has not been completed yet and the sanctions committee has not yet ratified (foodstuffs) purchasing deals," Thawra said.

Iraq, under the deal signed with the U.N. last May, started on December 10 limited oil sales worth $2 billion every six months to buy supplies for its population, suffering from stringent U.N. sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
"Why all this delay and procrastination?...Who is benefiting from this delay?," the paper asked.
